clue.text: It's round 17

definitions.meaning: something round in shape, like a ring or disc
the answer to 17 down, a piece of advertising post sent to many homes at once

explanation.surface: A terse remark that something is round, pointing to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 down is MAILSHOT, a batch of advertising letters; a leaflet sent round to everyone is also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for ring-shaped as an adjective, and as a noun a printed notice sent to many people at once.

clue.text: Overheard two thirds of security service is guarded

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the letters are said aloud and give a word that sounds like them

parts.note: the Soviet security service was the KGB; two of its three letters are K and G

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper picks up part of a spy agency's name and learns it is secretive.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters K and G come out as 'kay-gee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guarded is careful not to reveal much, which is the plain sense of this informal adjective for secretive.

clue.text: Accommodation's low rent initially raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters means reading them from bottom to top, so they run backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of rent is used

explanation.surface: A lodging comes with a low rent that has been put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective for cheap rent, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Space to stay in, such as a let bedroom, is a common sense of accommodation.

clue.text: American president takes line that's practical

indicators.note: the president takes the line into himself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a US president

explanation.surface: A US president adopts a sensible policy line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to be used in practice is serviceable, a near synonym of practical.

clue.text: High percent, on acid, likely to have a bad trip

definitions.text: likely to have a bad trip

indicators.note: being high on drugs leaves things jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone high on a large dose of LSD is liable to a bad trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad trip' plays on drug slang; the definition means one likely to stumble and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy often stumbles, so a bad trip, literally a fall, is a witty description of their tendency to mishaps.

clue.text: King interrupts subject to give some latitude

indicators.note: the king breaks into the subject, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch breaks in on a discussion to allow some freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' reads as leeway, but here it is a line on the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn are named parallels of latitude about 23 degrees from the equator.

clue.text: Touching a celibate woman, one who'll fight back

parts.note: RE means concerning or touching on, as in business letters
a nun, addressed as Sister, takes a vow of celibacy

explanation.surface: A man's advances on a nun are met with resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who opposes or refuses to submit is a fighter against force, as in a wartime resistance movement.

clue.text: Royal couple's courts

parts.note: Prince Philip, known as Phil, is one half of the royal couple
the couple is the pair joined: this one and that, the joining word
the other half is Elizabeth Regina, ER, here with the possessive 's

explanation.surface: The courts belonging to a king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal couple's' reads as Phil and ER's, Prince Philip and the Queen. 'courts' looks like royal palaces, but is a verb: flirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To court casually is to flirt and womanise, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Member of coalition getting near to forming a coalition?

parts.note: the UK's 2010 coalition government included the Conservatives, abbreviated Con
to be verging on something is to be getting near to it

explanation.surface: A coalition partner is close to joining forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2010 UK coalition was Conservative and Liberal Democrat. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or groups that meet and merge come together, which is a loose way of describing allies forming a pact.

clue.text: Diviner love cherished by men dancing with grace

indicators.note: something cherished is held close, so love goes inside the other letters
dancing moves the letters of men and grace around

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller adored by men waltzing with elegance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grace' reads as elegance and 'dancing' as the men's activity, but dancing is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of divination by marks in earth or patterns of dots is a kind of soothsayer.

clue.text: Bridle because setter provides stress

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's bridle and to rein in is to bridle
for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'
cement is something that sets hard

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker bristling with reasons causes strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but is a material that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis or strengthening added to a point is an accepted sense of stress.

clue.text: Kid with special trick taking one in

indicators.note: the trick takes the one into itself, so it sits inside
in confirms the one goes into the trick

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child with a particular sleight of hand that fools someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' and 'trick' suggest conning, but Kid here is the definition, a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant or heir of a family is its offspring, as a child is.

clue.text: Investment in capital? Add in scavenging for riches here

indicators.note: to be invested in something is to sit within it, so the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: Financial jargon about capital investment, then a pun on scavenging for wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The cave in the Arabian Nights story is a byword for a hoard of treasure.

clue.text: A poster plugging weak musical style

indicators.note: the pieces plug a gap inside another word

parts.note: rocky means shaky or weak
a bill is a poster stuck on a wall

explanation.surface: A poster promoting a feeble kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' reads as advertising, which suits a poster, but means filling.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1950s blend of rock and roll with country music is a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Property of fruit topped with pastry — go wrong with turnover

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece topped with another has that other above it

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
a date is a fruit of the palm

indicators.note: a turnover is turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit under pastry, then a wrong turn with a turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like another pastry, but it reverses ERR to RRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat or second home kept for occasional use is a piece of real estate.

clue.text: Writer's love movie

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
vid is short for video, a movie

explanation.surface: An author's romantic film.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Pound forged after Poles provided assistance for coppers

indicators.note: after says the jumbled word comes behind the poles and the condition

parts.note: the South and North poles, S and N
if means provided that

indicators.note: to pound something is to beat it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Polish counterfeit money helps the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money and 'Poles' like Polish people; Pound is the anagram signal, and Poles are the two ends of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use trained hounds to detect drugs and explosives, so the animal is an aid to officers.

clue.text: Newspaper's erotic advertising

parts.note: the Mail is a British newspaper, here with its possessive
hot can mean sexy or erotic

explanation.surface: A tabloid's racy adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulk posting of promotional material is a form of marketing sent by post.

clue.text: They seize someone's genetic material to implant in swimmers once

indicators.note: implanting puts one thing inside another, so the genetic code goes inside the fish

parts.note: kippers are smoked herrings, fish that swam once
DNA carries a person's genetic code

explanation.surface: A sinister lab story: stealing human DNA to put into fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmers once' means fish that are no longer alive: kippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Abductors take people by force, holding them for ransom.

clue.text: Country where Picaroon tried to get elected

parts.note: the setter is Picaroon, who refers to himself as I
to run for office is to stand for election

explanation.surface: The setter recalls a foreign election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic Republic in western Asia, formerly Persia, is a nation.

clue.text: Muscle spasm produces acid sort

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral muscle
a tic is an involuntary twitch or spasm

explanation.surface: A twitching muscle creates a type of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the acid derived from pectin, the gelling substance in fruit, so it names a kind of acid.

clue.text: One taking cap off batsman following balls

indicators.note: the batsman follows, so it comes second

parts.note: balls and bottle are both British slang for courage
an opener is a batsman who starts a cricket innings

explanation.surface: Cricket: a batter who removes his cap after facing some deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' suggests cricket balls but means nerve, British slang BOTTLE. An opener is one of the first two batsmen in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget for prising metal caps off drinks is the tool that removes the lid.

clue.text: In China, millions wanting return for capital

indicators.note: the letters return, coming back in reverse order
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Chinese money-saving story about lacking a return on millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' might suggest the slang for mate, but it just holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Peru, a national capital.

clue.text: Mistake, the 15th kind from reporter

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so a phrase is given as it would be heard

parts.note: O is the fifteenth letter, and kind is type, giving 'type O'

explanation.surface: A journalist's blunder about a certain kind of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type O' (also a blood group) said aloud sounds like the word for a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the keyboard is a printing error.

clue.text: Curl shot by goalposts for rugby pitch

indicators.note: shot here means wrecked or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H

explanation.surface: A curling kick past the posts on a rugby field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the rugby field, but is a verb, to lurch or toss as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to sway or roll suddenly, as a ship tossing in rough seas.

clue.text: Excite one female — pick extremely racy clothing

parts.note: to elect is to choose or pick

indicators.note: the ends of racy clothe the other letters, wrapping round them
extremely means only the first and last letters of racy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman picks a provocative outfit to thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely racy' reads as very daring, but takes the outside letters R and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill an audience is to galvanise it, as with an electric charge.

clue.text: French girl, back from Normandy, almost given the once-over

indicators.note: the back of Normandy is its last letter
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: vetted means checked over

explanation.surface: A girl returns from Normandy and is quickly checked out.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common female given name in France.

clue.text: Way of playing with pets round — and another pet round

indicators.note: turned round means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: cats are household pets
a cat is another household pet
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Playing with pets in a circle, then another pet joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' turns CATS backwards; the second is O.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for short, detached notes describes a manner of performance.
